item.title: Mike LaFleur: I know Carson Beck is prepared to go in if need be
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has earned a promotion.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has earned a promotion.

While Beck won't be starting this week, the quarterback shuffle stemming from Gardner Minshew's performance in Sunday's win over the Cowboys has elevated Beck from No. 3 to No. 2 on the team's depth chart.

Former starter Jacoby Brissett is now the No. 3 behind Beck, making him an obvious trade candidate.

How did Beck earn his new role?

“Obviously it’s just behind the scenes," head coach Mike LaFleur said in his Monday press conference. "Nothing that you guys see, but I know he’s prepared to go in there if need be. Again, just like Gardner, just like anyone that you ask that’s going to be on this team, they’re prepared as if they’re going to be the starting quarterback, or they’re prepared if they have to go in. I know that he has [a] full grasp of this game plan, [and] of this system.

"It’s no secret, obviously, if something were to happen, it’d be nice to know what we have right there. I feel really good about where he is with his development, so if that were to come up, then obviously he’d be the next one in.”

Beck had an impressive preseason debut in the Hall of Fame Game back in August. But he suffered a rib injury in that game that sidelined him for the rest of the exhibition contests that month. He has also recently dealt with a back issue.

After Beck was selected in the third round of this year's draft, it seems likely that his time to start for Arizona could be coming sooner rather than later — unless Minshew Mania leads the Cardinals to a long string of victories.

item.title: Dan Campbell credits Mike Kafka for big play to Amon-Ra St. Brown
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Lions ran what may have been the most inventive play of the week in the NFL when wide receiver Amon-Ra St.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions ran what may have been the most inventive play of the week in the NFL when wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown lined up 15 yards behind the line of scrimmage and got a running start of about 10 yards before Jared Goff threw him the ball, meaning that St. Brown was at full speed by the time the Vikings' defense had a chance to touch him. St. Brown gained 10 yards on the play.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket that Lions passing game coordinator Mike Kafka came up with that play.

"That was Kafka's baby. Like most plays, somebody gets an idea, and then you start massaging it, you slap it against the wall, 'What about this?' and everyone picks away at it," Campbell said. "We all have ideas and you throw them against the wall and it's either perfect or you start massaging it a little bit, you start tinkering. But that one started from Kafka, it was awesome. We'd had it up a couple weeks, just hadn't run it yet, and this was a good week to do it."

It was a great time to do it, and now the Lions' upcoming opponents have something unique they have to be prepared for.

item.title: Broncos overtake Chiefs as favorites in AFC West
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: There's a new favorite to win the AFC West.
item.content:encoded:
There's a new favorite to win the AFC West.

After beating the Chiefs on Sunday and improving to 6-2 on the season, the Broncos are now the betting favorites to win the division, for the first time this season.

The Broncos' odds to win the division are at -130. The Chiefs are close behind at +115. The Raiders are very long shots at +2500 and the winless Chargers are extreme long shots at +15,000.

The Chiefs had spent this season as the favorites, especially after blowing out the Broncos in Week 1. But the Chiefs are now on a two-game losing streak, and at 5-2 a half game behind the Broncos in the division.

The AFC West looks like it's going to be a two-horse race that goes deep into the season. At the moment, it's the Broncos who have the edge.

item.title: Dan Campbell: Jack Campbell is "improving"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Lions coach provides update on Jack Campbell's health following neck injury.
item.content:encoded:
The information out of Detroit regarding the status of linebacker Jack Campbell continues to be general. Regardless, the general message from Lions coach Dan Campbell on Tuesday morning was positive.

"The good news is he is improving," Dan Campbell said regarding Jack Campbell on 97.1 The Fan.

Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury early in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over the Vikings. He was taken to the hospital, and he remains there.

Dan Campbell also was asked about the impact of the Jack Campbell injury on the rest of the team.

"Well, I think the thought of him — knowing he's doing better — you know, and I've kept the captains up to date and they've let the other guys know is good news," Dan Campbell said.

In the absence of specifics, there will continue to be a sense of significant concern among the football community. For now, we'll continue to monitor the situation, share any updates, and hope that Jack Campbell continues to improve.

item.title: Caleb Williams has arrived as a top-tier quarterback
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Make room for the Bears QB in the Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow club.
item.content:encoded:
In recent weeks, Simms and I have raised once or twice the question of whether Bears quarterback Caleb Williams belongs in the top tier of NFL franchise quarterbacks.

Based on Monday night's 34-point performance against a Seahawks defense that held the Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes to three points a week earlier, it's time to render a verdict.

Yes.

The new top four, in our view, are (in no particular order), Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow, and Caleb Williams.

Lamar Jackson previously had been the fourth. A lost season due to multiple injuries puts him at No. 5, until he reestablishes himself in 2027. (And there's no reason to believe he won't, if he can get and stay healthy.)

For now, Caleb has crashed the party.

In Week 7 at Seattle, Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. His passer rating for the game was 58.9. In Week 8 at Seattle, Williams went 24 for 34 for 247 yards, one touchdown, and no picks. Williams also sparked a 39-yard gain on a key third-down backward pass to receiver Khalif Raymond, which set up the score that turned a 20-17 margin into a 27-17 clincher.

And before anyone says Mahomes didn't have any support in the running game, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III and Bears running back D'Andre Swift averaged an identical 2.6 yards per carry against the Seahawks' defense.

So, yes, Caleb is a top-level NFL quarterback. Despite missing three games with a hamstring injury, his odds to win the NFL MVP award are down to 5-1, behind only Allen, Brock Purdy, and Burrow.

If the Bears keep doing what they did on Monday night — and if they finish the season with the No. 1 seed in the NFC — Williams will get plenty of votes. And he has a real chance to win it.

Even if he'd much rather win the MVP award not for the regular season, but for the Super Bowl.

item.title: Bengals place DE Cashius Howell on injured reserve
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals announced that rookie defensive end Cashius Howell had wrist surgery on Monday, but head coach Zac Taylor said he didn't have a specific timeline for Howell's return to action.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals announced that rookie defensive end Cashius Howell had wrist surgery on Monday, but head coach Zac Taylor said he didn't have a specific timeline for Howell's return to action.

That timeline got a little clearer on Tuesday. The Bengals announced that Howell has been placed on injured reserve and will have to miss at least four games before he's able to get back into the lineup.

Howell was a second-round pick this year. He had six tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and five quarterback hits while playing around 40 percent of the defensive snaps in Cincinnati's first seven games.

The Bengals have not made a move to fill Howell's spot on the roster. Myles Murphy, Boye Mafe, Cedric Johnson, and Shemar Stewart are their other defensive ends.

item.title: Ben Johnson: Jeffery Simmons has fit right in, he got a game ball
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Fresh off last week's trade from the Titans to the Bears, defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons had a clear impact on Monday night's win over the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh off last week's trade from the Titans to the Bears, defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons had a clear impact on Monday night's win over the Seahawks.

Simmons finished the game with six tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack, and a pass defensed in the 34-17 victory.

Head coach Ben Johnson told reporters after the game that he gave Simmons a game ball or the performance.

“Our guys were excited the moment they heard the news we were bringing him on, and he's fit right in,” Johnson said. "We have a high-character locker room, and he's that himself. You can feel his presence out there, whether it's during the play or even after the play. You can feel him talk a little smack as well which I think that elevates everybody around him.

“I thought he played outstanding. He got one of the game balls. To come in there and have a share of the lead of tackles and a sack in his first game, his impact was profound.”

The Bears allowed just 252 total yards on Monday night, which was 1 yard off from Seattle’s lowest output of the season. The Bears will be at home to play the Buccaneers on Sunday night in Week 9.

item.title: Aaron Glenn on job security: I understand the business, but only think about the team
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets' loss to the Raiders in Week 8 dropped them to 2-6 and it left their record since hiring head coach Aaron Glenn at an unimpressive 5-20.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets' loss to the Raiders in Week 8 dropped them to 2-6 and it left their record since hiring head coach Aaron Glenn at an unimpressive 5-20.

Five of their six losses this season have come by one score, including all three on their current losing streak, and all of those results have contributed to increased speculation about how much longer Glenn is going to be in the job. During a Monday press conference, Glenn was asked how concerned he is that the Jets might decide to make a change.

"There's so much that I think about when it comes to us improving each week that that really doesn't come across my mind to be honest with you," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "I understand how this league is, I understand what this business is about, but my first job is each week of improving this team and that's the only thing that I think about."

Glenn did make it clear that he understands there need to be concrete signs of improvement soon.

"Absolutely. I mean, that's what this is," Glenn said. "It's a bottom-line business and we have to win, but we still have nine games left, so we still have an opportunity to win nine games."

That opportunity starts in Kansas City this week and missing out on it will only turn the heat under Glenn's seat higher.

item.title: Jerry Jones wants to see more targets for George Pickens
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems.
item.content:encoded:
The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems. During the first of his two weekly radio spots on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, owner and G.M. Jerry Jones mentioned one specific thing that he'd like to see change.

Regarding receiver George Pickens, Jones said this, via Jon Machota of The Athletic: "He needs the ball coming his way more."

Through eight games, Pickens has 62 targets. In Week 8 against the Cardinals, Pickens had the ball thrown in his direction only four times. Against the Eagles in Week 7, Pickens had six targets.

He has 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns in 2026. That projects to 83 catches for 1,132 yards and 8.5 touchdowns.

In 2025, Pickens finished with 93 receptions, 1,429 yards, and nine scores.

Hovering over the situation is the decision the Cowboys will have to make after the season. He's making $27.298 million under the franchise tag; they could tag him again next year, at $32.758 million. Which is still nearly $10 million behind the top of the receiver market.

There's another option, now that the Cowboys are fading in the race for the NFC East title. They could make Pickens available in trade.

Would a contender offer a second-round pick for him? The Chiefs are currently desperate for help at receiver; they're interested (we're told) in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Colts receiver Josh Downs. If the Chiefs are in on Pickens, other teams in the AFC (like the Bills) should be thinking about it, too.
bi
If the Cowboys were to decide to make a move, they could stockpile a pick or two — and save $15.17 million in cash and cap space. For now, who knows? The Cowboys seem to be deluding themselves into thinking they're still contenders.

Unless that's just part of the annual effort to keep their fans coughing up cash for tickets and merch. Which continues to work very well, relative to the on-field production.

For 31 years, and counting.

item.title: PFT's Week 9 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bills strengthen their grip on the top spot.
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 1; 6-1): The defense is getting better, but the offense took a little while to get going.

2. Jaguars (No. 2; 5-2): They caught the Colts at the perfect time, and they're catching the Ravens at the perfect time.

3. 49ers (No. 4; 6-1): Was the bye enough time for Christian McCaffrey to get healthy?

4. Broncos (No. 6; 6-2): They out-chiefed the Chiefs.

5. Bears (No. 8; 6-2): The Bears are NOT who we thought they were — they're serious contenders to win the whole thing.

6. Vikings (No. 3; 6-1): A quarterback change may be needed.

7. Chiefs (No. 5; 5-2): Can the Chiefs beat the best teams in the league?

8. Steelers (No. 10; 6-2): The schedule is lining up favorably; a 12-win season isn't out of the question.

9. Seahawks (No. 7; 4-4): Between last year's NFC finalists (Seahawks and Rams), one of them may not make it back to the playoffs. And maybe both.

10. Patriots (No. 11; 5-3): They avoided the South Florida trap, again.

11. Bengals (No. 12; 5-2): Joe Burrow is emerging as a serious MVP candidate.

12. Lions (No. 13; 5-2): The injuries are piling up on defense, again.

13. Browns (No. 9; 5-3): Jared Verse should've learned a lesson, but probably didn't.

14. Packers (No. 14; 5-3): The running game remains a liability.

15. Rams (No. 16; 4-4): The wins are happening, and Myles Garrett is lurking.

16. Giants (No. 17; 4-2-1): Will they go all-in for a high-end running back?

17. Raiders (No. 19; 4-4): A Kirk Cousins-Kyle Shanahan reunion game is looming.

18. Buccaneers (No. 20; 3-5): In two full games since returning from a thumb injury, Baker Mayfield has thrown 14 passes.

19. Ravens (No. 15; 4-4): Should they be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline?

20. Cardinals (No. 25; 3-5): They should move to Dallas. Or to L.A.

21. Falcons (No. 18; 3-5): It's a good thing they play in a dome.

22. Panthers (No. 22; 3-4): Add them to the list of teams that will be chasing Mike Tomlin.

23. Texans (No. 23; 2-5): The margin for error is getting smaller all the time.

24. Commanders (No. 30; 2-4-1): Backward Hat Energy.

25. Saints (No. 24; 2-5): They're still very much alive to win the worst division in the NFL.

26. Cowboys (No. 21; 3-5): Offseason hype, in-season tripe.

27. Eagles (No. 26; 2-6): That Super Bowl win from two years ago feels like it was two decades ago.

28. Titans (No. 27; 1-7): Unlike the Colts, the white-flag trade of Jeffery Simmons didn't cause them to quit.

29. Colts (No. 28; 2-6): Trade everyone.

30. Dolphins (No. 29; 1-6): Malik Willis has had two solid games in a row.

31. Jets (No. 31; 2-6): Everyone except Woody Johnson knows it's time for a coaching change.

32. Chargers (No. 32; 0-7): Jim Harbaugh's stubborn refusal to change coordinators could cost him his job.

item.title: Ravens add QB Austin Reed to practice squad
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: With starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley going down during Sunday’s loss to the Bills, the Ravens have brought in another quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
With starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley going down during Sunday’s loss to the Bills, the Ravens have brought in another quarterback.

Baltimore announced the team has signed Austin Reed to its practice squad.

Reed, 26, spent time with the Ravens in training camp after playing for the UFL’s Dallas Renegades in the spring.

Reed had previously played under Baltimore offensive coordinator Declan Doyle in 2025 when Doyle served in the same position with Chicago.

Baltimore is expected to start third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano in Thursday night’s game against Jacksonville, as Jackson may be out for the season and Huntley is reportedly dealing with turf toe.

Fagnano made his debut on Sunday, completing 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards with an interception in the loss to the Bills.

To add Reed, the Ravens released fullback Lucas Scott from its practice squad.

item.title: Teams are interested in Titans RB Tony Pollard, but Tennessee isn't talking (yet)
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After consistently telling teams that defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons would not be traded, the Titans decided last Tuesday to listen to offers.
item.content:encoded:
After consistently telling teams that defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons would not be traded, the Titans decided last Tuesday to listen to offers.

This Tuesday, they have another decision to make about one of the key offensive players on the roster.

Multiple teams are interested in running back Tony Pollard. So far, however, G.M. Mike Borgonzi has declined to engage in conversations about a potential trade.

Whether that will change remains to be seen, with or without someone calling owner Amy Adams Strunk directly.

Regardless, Pollard is an attractive option for any contender looking for help at the position. His contract is very affordable, relative to the veteran market. His 2027 base salary is $5.99 million (with $3.32 million left for 2026). In 2027, he's due to earn a non-guaranteed base salary of $6.74 million. (In each year, he earns $30,000 for each game in which he's on the active roster.)

Over the past two games, Pollard has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns. He's averaging in those two games 5.34 yards per carry.

Pollard has four straight 1,000-yard seasons (two with the Cowboys, two with the Titans). At 595 yards through eight games, he's on pace for a fifth.

With multiple teams linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor — and with the Colts not yet in a ballpark that will get a deal done — Pollard could become a much more affordable Plan B as the trade deadline creeps closer and closer.

item.title: The Vikings should explore a trade for Daniel Jones
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Kevin O'Connell's decision to punt with 3:01 to play speaks volumes about the level of trust in Kyler Murray.
item.content:encoded:
At a time when the Vikings are believed to be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor, they should adjust their focal point, just a bit.

The Vikings should be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for quarterback Daniel Jones.

When the thought first popped into my somewhat relaxed brain on Sunday, I was mostly kidding. After reflecting on Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions — and revisiting the rare displays of frustration from receiver Justin Jefferson late in the game and, even more significantly, from coach Kevin O'Connell when talking to quarterback Kyler Murray after an ugly interception late in the first half — it's not a joke.

They should immediately pivot from Taylor to Jones.

The Vikings had Jones in the building two years ago, after he was released by the Giants. They wanted to keep him for 2025, more (by all appearances) than they wanted to keep Sam Darnold. (Indeed, there were whispers of a potential benching of Darnold for Jones in the 2024 postseason.)

Now that the Colts are in full-blown pre-rebuild mode, trading Jones should be part of the effort to clear the decks (and stockpile picks) for the next G.M. And while the Colts have a window to avoid more than $10 million of Jones's $38 million compensation package for 2027 via a trade in the early days of the new league year in March, they could get more now from a contender that envisions Jones as an immediate upgrade.

Jones obviously won't be the long-term answer in Indianapolis. And he would undoubtedly welcome the chance to move on from a team that prematurely threw in the towel last week by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

In Minnesota, Jones would be an immediate upgrade over Kyler Murray. The difference between Jones vs. Murray could be more significant than the difference between Jonathan Taylor and Aaron Jones/Jordan Mason. Which, if accurate, would result in a bigger overall bump to the offense.

The Vikings have a championship-caliber defense, thanks in large part to the work of defensive coordinator Brian Flores. The grind-it-out-and-get-a-win formula had been working — until it didn't.

Here's the inescapable reality. When they win with quarterback play that is inconsistent and, in turn, frustrating to people like Jefferson and O'Connell, it's easy to overlook the flaws and keep pushing forward. When they lose, the frustrations of that moment become compounded by the lingering frustrations regarding plays and points left on the field in the wins that were salvaged by the defense.

Whether it's Jones or someone else (including a possible pivot to Carson Wentz), O'Connell and G.M. Nolan Teasley need to conduct a frank, candid, and objective assessment of the quarterback play under Murray. The fact that they picked Murray over J.J. McCarthy shouldn't be a factor. That's the kind of pride/ego consideration that keeps dysfunctional teams dysfunctional by doubling down on a mistake instead of admitting it and moving on.

The Vikings need to realize that: (1) the defense is great; (2) the running game is good enough; and (3) the passing game is too spotty to be expected to make a big play in a big spot.

Consider the decision that O'Connell made with 3:01 to play on Sunday, when the Vikings faced fourth and five from their own 33. Down four points after the Detroit running game had hot-knife-through-buttered their way to the go-ahead touchdown, why give the ball back to the Lions and let them close out the game by continuing to lean on Jahmyr Gibbs?

In that moment, O'Connell thought the chances of winning were enhanced by punting — not by asking the offense to gain five yards in a gotta-have-it situation.

While the choice showed unwarranted confidence in the defense, it showed NO confidence in the quarterback.

Frankly, that one specific decision from O'Connell leads naturally to the next, more consequential decision that the organization must make. If O'Connell doesn't trust the offense under Murray to gain five yards with the game on the line, the Vikings should no longer entrust the offense to Murray.

It's that simple. And, if the Vikings hope to avoid an outcome to the season that will result in an every-other-year playoff appearance and another one-and-done postseason, they'll make the decision that someone other than Murray should be playing quarterback.

At a time when politics have become a major national focal point, this would be a so-called 80-20 issue among Vikings fans. They've seen the "just good enough is just good enough" movie for decades. With the defense the Vikings currently have, the offense needs more. If they're serious about having a snowball's chance in San Diego to get back to the Super Bowl for the first time in 50 years, they'll send Kyler to Belize and make a play for Jones.

Or someone else. See if the Raiders are willing to part with Kirk Cousins (they shouldn't be, but why not make the call?) Call the Chargers about Justin Herbert. Scour every depth chart and start doing the due diligence.

When Cousins suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon just before the trade deadline in 2023, the Vikings mobilized instantly to find a replacement. Based on the full body of work from Murray to date in 2026, they should be doing the same thing now — if they want to parlay their 6-0 start into the best possible finish.

item.title: Aaron Glenn says Jets aren't trading Breece Hall
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game with a quad injury on Sunday and Braelon Allen continued to shine in his absence.
item.content:encoded:
Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game with a quad injury on Sunday and Braelon Allen continued to shine in his absence.

Allen ran 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown in the 38-33 loss to the Raiders and he's averaging just over 100 yards a game while Hall has been out of the lineup. Hall has practiced the last two weeks and he's been scratched after being listed as questionable, which has joined Allen's performance as reasons for some to wonder if the Jets might be thinking about trading Hall ahead of the November 10 deadline.

At a Monday morning press conference, head coach Aaron Glenn said that will not happen.

"Breece is still a part of this team," Glenn said, via Zack Rosenblatt of TheAthletic.com. "I've said it before: We're in the business of keeping good players and he's one of our better players so he'll be here."

The Jets have also reportedly rebuffed overtures from teams interested in trading for wide receiver Garrett Wilson, so it does not appear that their 2-6 start is going to lead to a fire sale over the next week.

item.title: Bears felt "profound" impact from Jeffery Simmons in his debut
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Simmons made an immediate impact for his new team.
item.content:encoded:
Jeffery Simmons had a sack early in Monday night's game in Seattle, but the defensive tackle's coaches and teammates made it clear after the 34-17 win that his impact on the Bears went deeper than his statistics.

The Seahawks averaged three yards per play when Simmons was on the field Monday night and the attention that Seattle paid to blocking him opened up avenues for other Bears defenders to make plays. Linebacker T.J. Edwards said that "you can feel his presence" on every play and defensive end Montez Sweat said he's "looking forward to taking advantage" of how offenses shift their attention to Simmons for the rest of the season.

That all adds up to what head coach Ben Johnson called Simmons's "profound" impact on the team and wide receiver Kalif Raymond said that it extended to the sideline as well.

"We're always watching the Jumbotron, but we were really watching the Jumbotron," Raymond said, via the team's website. "Watching him play, watching the impact he has, I mean, he has a whole other element."

The Bears gave up a lot to bring Simmons to Chicago and the first returns on the trade were nothing but positive.

item.title: Shane Steichen: Daniel Jones remains Colts' starter, gives us the best chance to win
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Colts coach Shane Steichen says he isn't benching quarterback Daniel Jones.
item.content:encoded:
Colts coach Shane Steichen says he isn't benching quarterback Daniel Jones.

Steichen said today that he still believes Jones is the best quarterback on the team, even after a dismal performance in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars dropped the Colts to 2-6.

"I feel that Daniel gives us the best chance to win right now," Steichen said.

On Sunday, Steichen benched Jones late in the game and gave Anthony Richardson his first playing time of the season. Richardson threw two passes, completing both of them for eight yards, and also took a sack that lost 10 yards. Richardson also had a five-yard run.

The Colts have already traded away two starters and would surely be willing to trade either Jones or Richardson if any other team wants them, but for now Steichen says he's coaching to win, and that Jones gives him the best chance to win.

item.title: Mike Macdonald: We lost in all three phases
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Monday night's game in Seattle featured a pair of 2025 NFC playoff teams who would like to be back in the postseason this year and it ended with the Bears celebrating a 34-17 win over the defending Super Bowl champions.
item.content:encoded:
Monday night's game in Seattle featured a pair of 2025 NFC playoff teams who would like to be back in the postseason this year and it ended with the Bears celebrating a 34-17 win over the defending Super Bowl champions.

The Seahawks had made it a three-point game early in the fourth quarter, but a 39-yard screen pass to Kalif Raymond converted a key Bears third down on the next drive and the roof caved in on the Seahawks from there. The Bears ended the night with 111 more offensive yards than the Seahawks and their defense thwarted Seattle on 10 of their 11 third down attempts over the course of the night, which led Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald to say after the game that "there's no other way to sugarcoat" the way his team got beat.

Seahawks kicker Jason Myers missed an extra point and had a field goal blocked and the Seahawks committed several personal fouls to add to their woes on a night when the Bears were clearly better across the board.

"They made it happen, and we didn't," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "It's a team effort; we lost as a team. In all three phases, we can have better plans, we can coach it better, prepare our players better, and we can play better. We'll go back to work and go attack the heck out of it. The margins in our league are too small, and when you don't do the things that it takes to win, that's how a game like that shapes up. It was a team effort. We lost in all three phases."

The Seahawks overwhelmed the Chiefs in a Week 7 win, but Monday night was the kind of step back that explains why they're 4-4 on the season. Having it happen against another NFC contender at home makes the blow more painful and Macdonald said the Seahawks "have some work to do" if they're going to position themselves for another run at the end of this season.

item.title: Lions lost linebacker Jimmy Rolder to season-ending hamstring injury vs. Vikings
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder will miss the rest of the season after suffering a hamstring injury on Sunday against the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder will miss the rest of the season after suffering a hamstring injury on Sunday against the Vikings.

Rolder's injury has been largely overlooked because it happened on the same play as the very scary injury suffered by linebacker Jack Campbell, who remains hospitalized. Rolder's injury isn't as serious but is a big one for the Lions, as Rolder is a rookie who had been playing an increasingly important role on Detroit's defense. Rolder was the Lions' leading tackler in their win over the Vikings.

"Jimmy Rolder is going to require surgery, or he could, this is a significant injury, he'll be out for the season," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said.

A fourth-round pick out of Michigan, Rolder has also been one of the Lions' top special teams players this season. The Lions suffered several injuries on Sunday, including two different plays when two different defensive players were knocked out of the game. Dan Campbell said the Lions had to rally to finish the game strong without several key players.

"Everybody goes through it and it's our time," Campbell said. "We overcame a lot of adversity, so I was proud of that, too."

Rolder will go on injured reserve. Campbell said the Lions' other injured players are still being evaluated for this week.

item.title: Jeffery Simmons: Felt great to get my first sack as a Chicago Bear
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "The emotions, especially during the national anthem, the emotions were coming and coming," Simmons said.
item.content:encoded:
It didn't take long for Jeffery Simmons to get his first sack as a Bear.

Simmons took Sam Darnold down on the Seahawks' fourth offensive play on Monday night, and he said afterward that as soon as he saw that they were blocking him one-on-one, he knew a big play was coming.

"If you block me one-on-one, I need to win the one-on-one. If I don't win a one-on-one, the coaches should be on me. I hold myself to a high standard," Simmons said. "It felt great to get my first sack as a Chicago Bear in my first game."

Simmons always drew a lot of double teams during his All-Pro seasons with the Titans, and he drew plenty on Monday night in his first game since the Titans traded him to the Bears as well. He said he challenged his fellow Bears defensive linemen to take advantage of it when he was getting double teamed.

"If I'm getting a double team, I expect them to win their single block," Simmons said. "We don't need to blitz. I feel like if we can win at the line of scrimmage without the blitzes, that makes the guys' jobs on the back end that much easier."

Simmons played 55 defensive snaps, by far the most of any Bear in the game. He played 87 percent of the Bears' defensive plays, which was exactly his snap count percentage for the Titans this season before he was traded. The Bears made a big investment in Simmons, trading two first-round draft picks for him, and they got a big return immediately.

In the moments before kickoff, Simmons said he was trying to keep his emotions in check by reminding himself, "It's just football." But it was hard not to be emotional.

"The emotions, especially during the national anthem, the emotions were coming and coming," Simmons said.

Simmons said after the game that it means a lot to him to be playing meaningful football. The Titans are 1-7 and the Bears are 6-2 and Simmons knows the blockbuster trade was an opportunity for him to compete for a Super Bowl.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray said he was dealing with hamstring tightness late in Sunday's loss to the Lions and his hamstring remains an issue on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray said he was dealing with hamstring tightness late in Sunday's loss to the Lions and his hamstring remains an issue on Monday.

Murray did not leave Sunday's game, but head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters at a press conference that the quarterback is dealing with soreness. Murray will be fully evaluated before the team makes any determination about his status for their Week 9 Monday night game against the Bills.

"I don't think we're there yet," O'Connell said.

O'Connell did say that the Vikings plan to start Murray against Buffalo as long as he is healthy enough to play. Speculation about a possible change has simmered as the Vikings offense struggled over the course of their 6-0 start and it has picked up in the wake of Minnesota's first loss of the season, but it doesn't look like they'll pull the trigger on any move as long as Murray is cleared to play this week.

item.title: Nick Sirianni: Eagles will stick with Tanner McKee, Sean Mannion despite offensive woes
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Eagles have lost six in a row and rank 30th in the NFL in points per game, but Nick Sirianni said Monday that he isn't making a change at offensive coordinator or quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles have lost six in a row and rank 30th in the NFL in points per game, but Nick Sirianni said Monday that he isn't making a change at offensive coordinator or quarterback.

Sean Mannion will continue to call plays, and Tanner McKee will remain the starting quarterback with Jalen Hurts out for the year.

"I'm not making any changes there," Sirianni said about his coaching staff, via Tim McManus of ESPN. "It is on all of us to figure out how to get things going in the right direction. Obviously, right now they're not. But again, this is the ultimate team game, and we're in the problem-solving business. Right now, we have to find answers to help us get going offensively. Again, that brunt falls on myself; that falls on Sean; and we're going to do everything we can to get ourselves out of this."

The first-year playcaller has had to make do without Hurts, right tackle Lane Johnson, center Cam Jurgens, running back Saquon Barkley and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks at times this season. Hurts played five games before going on injured reserve with blood clots; Johnson retired after three games; Jurgens played four games with the Eagles before a trade to the Ravens; Barkley has missed two games and been limited in others with injuries; Smith has missed four games with a hamstring injury; and Wicks has missed two games with an ankle injury.

The Eagles are averaging 17.1 points a game.

McKee has started the past three games, completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 639 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.

"Tanner's our guy. We're not making any changes there," Sirianni said. "Again, how do we find solutions? That could be within scheme; that could be within how our schedule is, practice plays. Everything's on the table for us in that aspect. But right now, this is where we are, and we're trying to find solutions there. We're looking at everything as far as what we can do differently as coaches."

McKee's backup, Joe Milton, only arrived in Philadelphia on Oct. 16, signing from the Cowboys' practice squad.

item.title: Caleb Williams chooses to "calm things down" in shoe dispute with NFL
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The battle lines were drawn, in the form of an $11,941 fine for Week 6 and a $23,882 fine for Week 7.
item.content:encoded:
The battle lines were drawn, in the form of an $11,941 fine for Week 6 and a $23,882 fine for Week 7. For Week 8, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams decided not to wear Caddix cleats that displayed the company's logo — and exposed him to another, even larger fine.

Based on the attached photo, Williams wore in Monay Caddix cleats that were made without any markings, thereby abandoning his ongoing fight with Big Shield.

"Just to calm things down, man," Williams told reporters after the 34-17 win over the Seahawks. "This was a big week, and [I'm] not here to, um, create any BS towards a team. You know, I want to keep that to a minimum for my side. Obviously, I get a lot of media.  And so, just try to minimize that as much as possible."

He had gone from daring the league to fine him, twice, to daring the league to keep him from playing in his footwear of choice. All along, the answer was hiding in plain sight — hide the name and logo of the company that made the cleats.

Williams still doesn't have a shoe deal, with Caddix or anyone else. Beyond reimbursing him for the fines (if the appeals fail), Caddix should be writing a sizable check to Caleb Williams. In one fell swoop, he gave the company far more exposure and positive publicity than the NFL's official shoe partners have gotten for the millions they've paid to have their logos on the piece of equipment that few if any viewers ever even notice.

item.title: Raiders to determine RB work by "who’s playing the best ball at the time"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When the Raiders drafted Ashton Jeanty with the sixth overall pick in 2025, the expectation was that he'd be their top choice in the backfield for years to come.
item.content:encoded:
When the Raiders drafted Ashton Jeanty with the sixth overall pick in 2025, the expectation was that he'd be their top choice in the backfield for years to come.

Jeanty has taken the most snaps of any of the team's running backs so far this season, but he averaged just over three yards a carry in the first seven games so the Raiders changed things up in Week 8. Mike Washington got more snaps than Jeanty and carried the ball 25 times while Jeanty ran it twice. Jeanty saw most of his playing time on passing downs and came up with a key 45-yard catch and run, but the shift in playing time remained a topic of conversation at head coach Klint Kubiak's Monday press conference.

Kubiak said it wasn't a permanent arrangement because decisions on playing time will be based on who the team feels is the top option at a given moment.

“I think it’s always a moving target,” Kubiak said. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner. That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.”

Kubiak pointed to Washington's practice work rather than Jeanty's sluggish production as the reason why he got bumped up in Sunday's rotation. Washington produced 83 yards on 25 carries, so it wasn't a major change in terms of success on the ground for the Raiders. It was a win after four straight losses, though, and that's usually a good argument for sticking with an approach the next time out.

item.title: Wil Lutz has made 113 straight extra points, most in the NFL since the 2015 rule change
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: It's been three years since Broncos kicker Wil Lutz missed an extra point.
item.content:encoded:
It's been three years since Broncos kicker Wil Lutz missed an extra point.

After hitting both his extra points in Sunday's win over the Chiefs, Lutz has now made 113 consecutive extra points without a miss. That's the longest streak in the NFL since the 2015 rule change that moved extra points back by 13 yards. The previous record of 112 consecutive extra points was set by Justin Tucker with the Ravens.

“I’ve [said] a hundred times how much I value the extra point. I value them a lot. But my goal isn’t to break the record, it’s to make every one the rest of the season, so whatever that number is at the end of the season," Lutz told Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette.

Lutz's last missed an extra point when he doinked one off the upright against the Bills on November 11, 2023. Lutz made up for that with the game-winning field goal as time expired in a 24-22 victory.

The 32-year-old Lutz first entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie in 2016 with the Ravens, who weren't seriously considering him for a roster spot as they had Tucker, who was the best kicker in the NFL at the time. But Lutz impressed then-Ravens coach John Harbaugh enough that when it came time to cut Lutz at the end of the preseason, Harbaugh personally called then-Saints coach Sean Payton to recommend Lutz. Payton brought Lutz to New Orleans, and then traded for Lutz when Payton became coach of the Broncos.

By having faith in Lutz, Payton has ensured that he'll have nothing to worry about on extra points.

item.title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline live updates: Tracker, deals, news, rumors, analysis
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and more big-name NFL players are on the move.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and PFT has you covered with news and analysis of every trade, potential trade, rumor of a trade and trade that won’t be happening.

Here’s what’s happening on the NFL trade front:

Chargers say they're not trading Khalil Mack: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said, "I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here."

Jeffery Simmons to Bears: Chicago receives Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tennessee will receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-round pick in 2027.

Quenton Nelson to Seahawks: The Seahawks will send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick back to Indianapolis.

DeForest Buckner to 49ers: Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from San Francisco.

Jonathan Taylor trade talks have picked up: The Colts may not be done making deals.

The Jets have reportedly rebuffed Garrett Wilson trade interest: The Jets are not expected to deal their top wideout.

The Colts are open for business: Indianapolis is building for the future after firing General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor hasn’t requested a trade. Josh Downs says he's "open to whatever."

Budda Baker's name surfaces in trade rumors: Baker says he hasn’t asked to be traded from Arizona and also hasn't asked not to be traded.

Brian Thomas is a name to watch: The Jaguars trading Thomas frequently comes up in trade rumors.

Garrett Wilson wants to remain a Jet: The talented receiver says he is hoping not to get traded.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh: I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jim Harbaugh shot down a question about the Chargers potentially trading defensive lineman Khalil Mack before next week's deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Jim Harbaugh shot down a question about the Chargers potentially trading defensive lineman Khalil Mack before next week's deadline.

“I want Khalil Mack here," Harbaugh said. "Khalil Mack wants to be here. He’s one of the pillars of our team.”

Harbaugh said he isn't even thinking about the November 10 trade deadline and is instead looking to get ready to play the Texans this week. Harbaugh said General Manager Joe Hortiz and Assistant General Manager Chad Alexander might be looking at trades, but he isn't.

"I'm focused on the Texans. I know Joe, Chad, our organization are always looking to improve the team," Harbaugh said. "I'm focused on getting it turned, forging ahead, striving in every way to play winning football."

The 0-7 Chargers are the NFL's only winless team, and at this point there's no trade that could make them playoff contenders in 2026. So whether Harbaugh is thinking about it or not, it seems likely that the Chargers would be willing to trade a player on their roster for a draft pick, if they get a decent offer in the next week.
